newsitem.title: UK: UK minister admits jobless figures bogus - Labour.
newsitem.headline: UK minister admits jobless figures bogus - Labour.

text.p: Britain's opposition Labour party said on Thursday that a government minister had admitted that official unemployment figures were "bogus".

Labour's employment spokesman, David Blunkett, seized on a report in the Financial Times quoting employment minister Eric Forth commenting on Wednesday's news that British unemployment fell 67,800 in January to the lowest rate for six years.
Forth was quoted as saying: "The nearest we can come to is that about half of these figures we are giving each month are genuine falls in unemployment."
Blunkett said: "This is a rare and amazing phenomenon, a Tory minister has told at least half the truth.
"But the question then arises, why are the Tories releasing so-called unemployment figures which they know to be bogus and why should anyone in future report them as anything but bogus...

"This is an admission of monumental proportions which confirms the cynicism and utter dishonesty which underlie the official unemployment figures," he said in a statement, adding that the government should explain the remarks to parliament.

The Labour party, well ahead in the polls with an election due in the next three months, has long accused Prime Minister John Major of "massaging" unemployment figures, with changes in the way benefit is calculated reducing the jobless total.
It has pledged to review the figures once in power.

In the Financial Times interview, Forth said recent big falls in unemployment were "a temporary phase" due to changes in benefit regulations, adding that the changes had "given these figures a boost in the short term".

But the government argues that the figures from the Office for National Statistics, which on Wednesday showed 1.82 million people were unemployed and seeking benefit compared to 1.88 million in December, show its economic policies are working.
